chunks: And Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Sa'id narrated to us, saying: Abu Muhammad Abdullah ibn Ahmad ibn al-Mustawrid al-Ashja'i narrated to us, saying: Muhammad ibn Ubaydillah Abu Ja'far al-Halabi narrated to us, saying: Abdullah ibn Bukayr narrated to us, from Zurara, who said: I heard Abu Abdullah Ja'far saying:

Indeed, for the Qa'im there is a ghaybah (occultation/disappearance) before he rises. I asked: 'Why is that?' He said: 'Indeed, he fears,' and he pointed with his hand to his abdomen, meaning killing.
ai.seo_question: Why did the Qa'im experience an occultation before his rise?
ai.summary: In this narration from Imam Ja'far al-Sadiq (as), the gesture towards his abdomen highlights the physical vulnerability and imminent threat of assassination that necessitates the Qa'im's hidden period. This establishes the pre-emergence occultation not merely as a divine plan, but as a pragmatic measure for survival against political enemies, a concept central to Shia eschatology regarding the Mahdi's timeline.

en.abdullah-al-shahin: (21) Ahmad bin Muhammad bin Sa’eed narrated from Abu Muhammad Abdullah bin Ahmad bin al-Mustawrid al-Ashja’iy from Muhammad bin Obaydillah Abu Ja’far al-Halabi from Abdullah bin Bukayr that Zurara had said: I heard Abu Abdullah Ja’far as-Sadiq (as) saying: “

Al-Qa’im disappears before his rising.” I asked: “Why?” He said: “He fears” and he pointed with his hand at his abdomen. He meant “killing”. The same was narrated by Muhammad bin Ya’qoob al-Kulayni from Muhammad bin Yahya from Ja’far bin Muhammad from al-Hasan bin Mo’awiya from Abdullah bin Jibilla from Abdullah bin Bukayr from Zurara from Abu Abdullah as-Sadiq (as).
